name: T4DM
aliases: Testosterone for the Prevention of Type 2 Diabetes
question: Does testosterone undecanoate added to a lifestyle programme prevent or revert diabetes-range glucose values in men at high metabolic risk?

arms.label: Intramuscular testosterone undecanoate plus lifestyle programme

design.population: Men aged 50–74 years with waist circumference ≥95 cm, screening testosterone ≤14.0 nmol/L without pathological hypogonadism, and 2-hour OGTT glucose 7.8 to <11.1 mmol/L or newly diagnosed diabetes with 2-hour glucose 11.1–15.0 mmol/L.
design.description: Six-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3b randomized trial; men at high cardiovascular risk or with baseline hematocrit >50% were excluded. Co-primary significance thresholds were 3.5% (categorical) and 2.5% (continuous); either could make the trial positive.
design.locator: Full text, Study design and participants, p 34

verdictNote: Both prespecified glucose outcomes met their allocated thresholds; hematocrit safety triggers were frequent.
takeaway: In T4DM, intramuscular testosterone undecanoate plus a lifestyle programme reduced diabetes-range 2-hour glucose and improved mean 2-hour glucose at 2 years versus placebo plus the same programme among participants with 21–27-month OGTT data; hematocrit at least 54% triggered safety review more often with testosterone.

results.measure: 2-hour glucose ≥11.1 mmol/L at 2 years among participants with 21–27-month OGTT data, analysed by intention-to-treat assignment
results.note: Available-outcome intention-to-treat analysis included participants who stopped treatment or began diabetes medication; post-hoc multiple-imputation sensitivity RR 0.62 (95% CI 0.47–0.82; P=0.0015).

results.measure: Mean change from baseline at 2 years; between-arm mean difference in mmol/L
results.note: Negative difference favors testosterone; available-outcome intention-to-treat analysis.

harms.label: Hematocrit safety trigger ≥54%
harms.note: Masked monitoring; confirmed elevation permanently stopped treatment in 25 testosterone and one placebo participant.

harms.label: PSA increase safety trigger ≥0.75 μg/mL
harms.note: Masked monitoring; rise prompted repeat testing and possible urologic assessment.

harms.label: Prespecified serious adverse events
harms.locator: Full text, Table 5 and Results, p 41
harms.note: Two deaths in each group; participants with any cardiovascular event: 26/504 versus 21/503.

harms.label: Selected prespecified serious adverse event categories

values.ctl: BPH-related hospital admissions 3/503; prostate cancer 5/503; venous thromboses 0/503

harms.note: Table 5 reports event counts; no participant had more than one event in a given subcategory.

delivery.label: Injection schedule
delivery.value: Testosterone undecanoate 1,000 mg (4 mL) or matching placebo injected slowly and deeply into the upper outer gluteal muscle at baseline, 6 weeks, then every 3 months for 2 years; no dose or interval adjustment. Both groups enrolled in a lifestyle programme.

delivery.label: Treatment completion and lifestyle adherence

values.exp: 386/504 completed 2 years of treatment; 116/504 discontinued early; 144/480 (30%) reported lifestyle-programme adherence at 2 years
values.ctl: 370/503 completed 2 years of treatment; 131/503 discontinued early; 132/471 (28%) reported lifestyle-programme adherence at 2 years

delivery.locator: Full text, Figure 1, p 36; Results, p 39; Table 3, p 39
delivery.note: Lifestyle adherence meant self-reported website use, meeting attendance, or both since the previous visit.
